name: Akamai Technologies, Inc.
reason: Mid-transition from a maturing CDN to security/cloud compute with EBIT margin down from 23.3% (2021) to 14.9%, net debt/EBITDA 3.4x and an 83% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap, so the 5-10 year mix and margin path cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Truist Financial Corp.
reason: Merger-built bank with only 4.0% 10y EPS CAGR, shares up 5.6%/yr, 6.6% average ROE and a 2023 goodwill-driven loss; no specialness and growth has come from M&A not the core franchise.

name: CVB Financial Corp.
reason: High-quality low-cost-deposit, conservatively underwritten bank, but EPS has been flat near $1.5 since 2021 (5.0% 10y CAGR with shares +2.6%/yr) so there is no plausible route to 7%+ EPS growth.

name: Del Monte Corp.
reason: Commodity fresh-produce grower with 3.5% average EBIT margin and 3.8% average ROIC; EPS volatile (worst year -82%) and driven by crop/freight costs no one can forecast.

name: Unum Group
reason: Group disability/life earnings at 0.96x 10y peak on record-low disability incidence, plus a closed-block long-term-care tail risk that makes the 10-year outcome hard to underwrite despite buybacks (shares -3.5%/yr).

name: NetScout Systems, Inc.
reason: Shrinking revenue (-1.1%/yr over 10 years), negative average ROIC and a 181% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap; EPS growth comes from cost cuts, not a durable franchise.

name: The Charles Schwab Corp.
reason: Scale low-cost leader with real asset-gathering momentum, but EPS (1.0x 10y max) and EBIT margin (46.9%, 100th percentile) are at peak and driven by interest rates on sweep cash and market levels, as the 2023 -20% EPS drop showed.

name: Jefferies Financial Group, Inc.
reason: Investment bank whose earnings swing with capital-markets activity (EPS 5.86 in 2021 vs 1.10 in 2023, latest 0.48x 10y max) with net debt/EBITDA 4.6x.

name: Flagstar Bank NA
reason: Turnaround bank with losses in 2024 (-3.40) and 2025 (-0.50), shares up 10.7%/yr and concentrated NYC rent-regulated multifamily/CRE credit risk.

name: Independent Bank Corp. (Massachusetts)
reason: Sound Massachusetts commercial bank but growth is acquisition-led (shares +5.9%/yr over 10 years) and EPS is at 0.97x its 10y high with only 8.5% average ROE; ordinary, not special.

name: TriCo Bancshares
reason: Solid but ordinary California community bank: 6.9% 10y EPS CAGR helped by acquisitions (shares +3.6%/yr), EPS flat since 2021 at 0.94x peak and ~10% ROE.

name: OceanFirst Financial Corp.
reason: Acquisitive thrift with 1.0% 10y EPS CAGR against 13.1%/yr share growth and 6.8% average ROE; latest EPS 0.61x the 10y high.

name: Universal Corp.
reason: Leaf-tobacco merchant facing secular cigarette volume decline, EPS CAGR -10.5% over 10 years, 4.6% average ROIC and net debt/EBITDA 3.4x.

name: SSR Mining, Inc.
reason: Gold miner whose earnings are set by the gold price (EPS 1.0x 10y max at a commodity peak) with Copler mine-collapse operating/regulatory risk in Turkey and shares up 10.4%/yr.

name: First Commonwealth Financial Corp. (Pennsylvania)
reason: Ordinary Pennsylvania regional bank with ~10% ROE; the 10.1% 10y EPS CAGR starts from a depressed 2015 base and EPS has been flat near 1.4-1.5 since 2021 (0.95x peak).

name: Seacoast Banking Corp. of Florida
reason: Serial acquirer with shares up 10.2%/yr, EPS down from 2.36 (2021) to 1.84 and 7.6% average ROE; growth is from M&A not the core franchise.

name: Ovintiv, Inc.
reason: Oil and gas E&P whose earnings are set by commodity prices (EBIT margin -10% to +40% over the decade) with acquisitions at 0.92x of 10y FCF.

name: The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc.
reason: Much-improved commercial P&C and group-benefits franchise with 13.2% 10y EPS CAGR, but EPS 13.42 is at its 10y high near the top of the commercial pricing cycle with legacy asbestos/environmental reserves, so normalized earnings are hard to pin down.

name: SM Energy Co.
reason: Shale E&P with commodity-driven earnings (losses in 5 of 2015-2020, EBIT margin -41% to +58%) and a 99% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap.

name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
reason: Two strong brands (UGG, HOKA) with 25% 10y EPS CAGR and EPS up in 9 of 10 years, 25% average ROIC, net cash and steady buybacks (shares -3%/yr); margin at 91st percentile and HOKA deceleration/fashion risk need testing in the deep dive.
